Interactive Reference

Security+ SY0-701 Acronyms

Key security acronyms, expansions, and core concepts.

🔍
AAA

Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting - A core security framework used to manage access control, verify user identities, grant resource permissions, and log system activity.

AES

Advanced Encryption Standard - A modern, highly secure symmetric block cipher algorithm approved by NIST for protecting sensitive electronic data.

DES

Data Encryption Standard - An older, deprecated symmetric key algorithm with a 56-bit key size, now considered insecure and replaced by AES.

3DES

Triple Data Encryption Standard - A legacy symmetric encryption cipher that applies the DES algorithm three times to each data block, currently deprecated in favor of AES.

RSA

Rivest-Shamir-Adleman - One of the first widely used asymmetric cryptographic algorithms for secure data transmission and digital signatures.

PKI

Public Key Infrastructure - The framework of roles, policies, hardware, software, and procedures needed to create, manage, distribute, use, store, and revoke digital certificates.

MFA

Multi-Factor Authentication - A security system requiring multiple separate categories of credentials to verify a user's identity for login.

XSS

Cross-Site Scripting - A web security vulnerability that allows an attacker to inject malicious client-side scripts into web pages viewed by other users.

SQLi

SQL Injection - A vulnerability where malicious SQL statements are inserted into entry fields for execution (e.g., to dump database contents to the attacker).

HSTS

HTTP Strict Transport Security - A web server header forcing browsers to communicate only through secure HTTPS connections.

CSP

Content Security Policy - An HTTP header allowing site operators to restrict resources (JavaScript, CSS, Images) that the browser is allowed to load.

CA

Certificate Authority - A trusted organization that issues digital certificates to verify identity entities on the internet.

CRL

Certificate Revocation List - A list of digital certificates that have been revoked by the issuing CA before their scheduled expiration date.

CSR

Certificate Signing Request - An encoded message sent from an applicant to a CA in order to apply for a digital certificate.

CIA Triad

Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability - The core model designed to guide policies for information security within an organization.

IDS

Intrusion Detection System - A device or software application that monitors a network or systems for malicious activity or policy violations and reports alerts.

IPS

Intrustion Prevention System - An active network security device that monitors network traffic and proactively blocks discovered threats.

SIEM

Security Information and Event Management - A system that aggregates log data from multiple sources, analyzes it in real-time, and flags security alerts.

SAML

Security Assertion Markup Language - An XML-based open standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between identity providers and service providers (used for SSO).

OIDC

OpenID Connect - An identity layer built on top of the OAuth 2.0 framework, allowing clients to verify the identity of the end-user based on authentication.

OAuth

Open Authorization - An open standard authorization framework that provides secure delegated access for applications over APIs using tokens.

RBAC

Role-Based Access Control - A method of restricting system access to authorized users based on defined organizational roles.

ABAC

Attribute-Based Access Control - Access control model where rights are granted based on attributes (user, resource, environment) evaluated against security policies.

MAC

Mandatory Access Control - A strict access control system where the operating system constrains user rights based on security labels and clearances.

DAC

Discretionary Access Control - An access control model where the owner of a resource determines who is permitted access and what privileges they have.

CVE

Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures - A public, standardized list of publicly known information security vulnerabilities and exposures.

CVSS

Common Vulnerability Scoring System - An open framework for communicating the characteristics and severity scores (from 0 to 10) of IT vulnerabilities.

RTO

Recovery Time Objective - The target duration of time and service level within which a business process must be restored after a disaster or disruption.

RPO

Recovery Point Objective - The maximum tolerable age of data that must be recovered from backup storage for operations to resume after a disaster.

MTBF

Mean Time Between Failures - The average time elapsed between inhering failures of a system during normal system operation (measure of reliability).

MTTR

Mean Time to Repair - The average time required to repair a failed component or system and restore it to full operational status.

SLA

Service Level Agreement - A contract between a service provider and its customer that documents what services the provider will furnish and the performance standards expected.

BIA

Business Impact Analysis - A systematic process to determine and evaluate the potential effects of an interruption to critical business operations.

DLP

Data Loss Prevention - A set of tools and processes designed to ensure that sensitive data is not lost, misused, or accessed by unauthorized users.

VPN

Virtual Private Network - A service that creates a safe, encrypted connection over a less secure network, such as the public internet.

IPSec

Internet Protocol Security - A secure network protocol suite that authenticates and encrypts the packets of data sent over an IP network.

SSO

Single Sign-On - An authentication scheme that allows a user to log in with a single ID and password to any of several related, yet independent, software systems.

ACL

Access Control List - A list of rules that specifies which users or system processes are granted access to objects, or which network packets are allowed through.

MDM

Mobile Device Management - Software that allows IT administrators to control, secure, and enforce policies on smartphones, tablets, and other endpoint devices.

RADIUS

Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service - A networking protocol operating on port 1812/1813 providing centralized Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting management for users.

TACACS+

Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus - A proprietary Cisco protocol providing AAA services, separating authentication and authorization, running over TCP port 49.

DNSSEC

Domain Name System Security Extensions - A suite of extension specifications for securing certain kinds of information provided by the DNS using cryptographic signatures.

SFTP

Secure File Transfer Protocol - A secure version of File Transfer Protocol (FTP) that facilitates data access and data transfer over a Secure Shell (SSH) data stream on port 22.

FTPS

File Transfer Protocol Secure - An extension to FTP that adds support for the Transport Layer Security (TLS) and the Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) cryptographic protocols.

WPA3

Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 - The third generation of wireless security standards, providing improved cryptographic strength and protection against offline dictionary attacks (using SAE).

TPM

Trusted Platform Module - A specialized, tamper-resistant cryptographic microchip integrated into device motherboards to secure hardware with cryptographic keys.

HSM

Hardware Security Module - A physical computing device that safeguards and manages digital keys, performs encryption and decryption functions, and strong authentication.

DDoS

Distributed Denial of Service - A malicious attempt to disrupt normal traffic of a targeted server, service, or network by overwhelming the target or its surrounding infrastructure with a flood of Internet traffic from multiple sources (botnet).

APT

Advanced Persistent Threat - A stealthy threat actor, typically a nation-state or state-sponsored group, which conducts a continuous, highly targeted attack to establish and maintain access to a network.

Interactive Reference

Security+ SY0-701 Glossary

Key cryptographic terms and definitions. More terms will be added at a later date.

🔍
AAA Framework

A security framework standing for Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting used to manage access and track activity.

Accounting

The process within AAA that logs system events, including login/logout times and the amount of data sent or received.

AES (Advanced Encryption Standard)

A modern, widely-used symmetric encryption algorithm.

Asymmetric Encryption

A cryptographic method using a pair of keys: a private key known only to the owner and a public key available to anyone.

Authentication

The process of proving a claimed identity using passwords or other factors.

Authorization

The process of determining the specific resources or data a verified user is allowed to access.

Backout Plan

A documented contingency procedure used to revert a system to its original state if a change or update fails.

Baseline

A standard or goal used in gap analysis, often derived from organizations like NIST or ISO, to measure security progress.

CA (Certificate Authority)

A device or software responsible for managing and digitally signing certificates within a security infrastructure.

CIA Triad

The foundational model of IT security consisting of Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability.

Compensating Control

A security control used temporarily to mitigate a risk when the primary control (like a software patch) is unavailable.

Corrective Control

A security control applied after an event is detected to reverse the impact or restore systems, such as a data backup.

CRL (Certificate Revocation List)

A list maintained by a CA containing certificates that are no longer valid.

CSR (Certificate Signing Request)

A request sent from an applicant to a CA to obtain a signed digital certificate.

Data Masking

A technique used to hide sensitive data by replacing it with characters like asterisks.

DES (Data Encryption Standard)

An older symmetric encryption algorithm with five steps, now largely replaced by AES.

Deterrent Control

A security control designed to discourage an attacker, such as warning signs or splash screens.

Digital Signature

A cryptographic tool that provides non-repudiation by proving both the integrity of the data and the identity of the sender.

Gap Analysis

A study comparing the current security state of an organization to a desired future state or baseline.

Hash

A short string of text representing a "fingerprint" of data; used to verify that information has not been altered (integrity).

Honeyfile

A file containing fake but attractive information used to lure and detect unauthorized users on a network.

Honeynet

A complex infrastructure of virtualized honeypots (servers, routers, firewalls) designed to look like a real production network.

Honeypot

A system designed to attract and trap attackers or automated processes to observe their techniques.

Honeytoken

Traceable, fake data (like API credentials or email addresses) used to identify the source of data leaks.

HSM (Hardware Security Module)

A centralized hardware device used for high-speed cryptographic processing and key management.

Key Stretching

A method used to strengthen weak keys by repeating the hashing or encryption process multiple times.

Managerial Control

Security controls implemented through administrative policies and procedures.

Non-repudiation

The assurance that the sender of a message cannot deny having sent it, provided by digital signatures.

OCSP (Online Certificate Status Protocol)

A real-time protocol used to check the revocation status of a digital certificate.

Operational Control

Security controls implemented through human action, such as security guards or training programs.

Perfect Forward Secrecy / Ephemeral Keys

Temporary session keys that are used for a short time and then discarded.

Performance-Based Questions

CompTIA exam questions that require the candidate to perform a task or complete a process rather than selecting a multiple-choice answer.

Physical Control

Controls that limit physical access to buildings or devices, such as locks, fences, and badge readers.

PKI (Public Key Infrastructure)

The entire system of hardware, software, and policies used to manage digital certificates.

Rainbow Table

A pre-compiled list of plaintext passwords and their corresponding hashes used to quickly crack passwords.

Salt

Random data added to a plaintext password before hashing to ensure unique hash outputs.

Sandbox

A technological "safe space" or duplicate environment used for testing changes without affecting production systems.

Stakeholders

Individuals or departments impacted by a proposed change who provide input on its timing and implementation.

Symmetric Encryption

An encryption method that uses the same key for both encryption and decryption.

Technical Control

Security controls implemented through operating systems, software, or hardware, such as firewalls.

TPM (Trusted Platform Module)

A specialized chip on a computer's motherboard that provides hardware-based security functions.

X.509

The standard format defining the information contained within a digital certificate.
